channel.title: Maxwell changelog
channel.description: New features, fixes and improvements in Maxwell.

item.title: Cloud sessions
item.description:
Maxwell now works with Claude Code sessions that run on Anthropic's cloud machines. They sit in the same groups as your other sessions, marked cloud, and a question from one shows in Needs you with a notification. Opening one shows its claude.ai page in the middle pane, signed in to its account.

⌥⌘N starts a session in the cloud from a project and a task. With Cloud picked, the new-session panel says what won't go along, such as commits that aren't pushed. ⌥⌘↑ sends a session from your Mac to the cloud: it commits, pushes and writes a brief, and a cloud session continues from there. ⌥⌘↓ brings a cloud session back into a fresh worktree. How cloud sessions work.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed hovering over text in a session sending Claude Code stray pointer moves while Maxwell looked for a link
  • A path's underline no longer stays behind under other text when output or scrolling moves the text under a resting pointer
  • Maxwell now sends a report when it crashes or stops responding, scrubbed of paths, prompts and names, so crashes get fixed without anyone writing in. Settings › General › Send crash reports turns it off. What a report holds
  • Clicking an artifact link in a session's terminal now opens it in the viewer the first time, also when Maxwell is in the background. Before, the first click only brought the window forward, and the next one counted as a double click and opened the link in the browser
  • File paths in a session are now links: hover one and it's underlined, click it and the file opens in the viewer, no ⌘ needed
  • The folder now fills a narrow viewer when no file is open, instead of leaving a dimmed empty strip beside it
  • Terminals now come back after a restart, in the same folders and order, showing what they showed before, colours included, under a dim “restored” line; one whose folder is gone opens in the nearest folder still there
  • Terminals can now be renamed: double-click a terminal's row, or right-click it and pick Rename…; the name stays after a restart
  • Terminals now have tabs, like sessions, and closing a terminal's tab leaves it running in the sidebar
  • Search (⌘P) now finds terminals by name and folder
  • Rename… is now in the Session menu and in ⌘K, for the open session or terminal
  • Closing a terminal now offers Undo, which brings back what it showed, and asks first when a command is still running in it, naming the command
  • The window's corners are now round, instead of a stepped bevel inside the rim macOS draws

item.title: Safe to close trusts the session's own word
item.description:
When a session ends its reply with Safe to close and every other check passes (nothing running, git clean and pushed, the PR merged), it now goes straight to Safe to close. Before, Haiku read the reply once more and could hold it back as unsure or pending over a caveat or a note, and it answered differently for the same reply.

Replies without a status line still get the Haiku read.

item.title: Idle sessions free their memory
item.description:
Claude Code stops a background session that has been idle for about an hour, to free memory, but only when no terminal is attached to it. Maxwell used to keep every session you opened attached until it quit, so none of them were ever stopped. Now Maxwell lets go of a session's terminal after 10 minutes off screen, and attaches again when you open it.

A session Claude Code stopped while it waited on you stays in Your turn or Needs you. Opening it shows its last reply and a Resume button, so moving through the list doesn't start every session it passes. ⌘R resumes it too. Its conversation is kept, as always.

Fixes and improvements

  • Grey text is easier to read in every theme and now meets WCAG AA contrast
  • A session waiting on you no longer disappears from the list when Claude Code stops it

item.title: Agents that wait still count
item.description:
A subagent can start a long command, end its turn and wait for it. Claude Code reports that as done for now, so Maxwell stopped counting the agent and the row lost its agents note while the agent was still at work. Maxwell now keeps counting it until the agent really finishes.

Fixes and improvements

  • The header's agents button now stays at the right edge, so a long session title no longer hides it

item.title: Pin sessions, and overrule a verdict
item.description:
Right-click a session and choose Pin to Top. Pinned sessions are listed first, under Pinned, and Close all leaves them alone.

Mark As puts a session under Your turn, Safe to close or Idle when you disagree with Maxwell. The mark holds until the session's next turn. A session you mark safe says which checks still fail.

⇧⌘X now closes only the safe sessions of the project you're in, so a session from another project never lands in the list.

Fixes and improvements

  • Sessions that started before Maxwell asked for the status line now get the request with your next prompt

item.title: Side panels open one at a time
item.description: Panels on the same side now work like tabs. Opening the plugins panel closes the viewer beside it, and opening the viewer closes the plugins panel. The usage and system widgets at the bottom still sit side by side.

item.title: Start a session from any terminal's folder
item.description: Run open -a Maxwell . in any terminal, or drop a folder on Maxwell in the Dock, and the new-session panel opens with that folder picked. ⏎ starts the session there, so you don't need a terminal inside Maxwell to start in the right place.

item.title: Claude in a Maxwell terminal is one row
item.description:
Run claude in a terminal you opened in Maxwell (⌥⌘T) and that terminal's row becomes the session's: its title, its group, Needs you and Your turn. Before, the terminal and the session showed up as two rows, and the session's pane was read-only even though it ran right there.

The pane shows the terminal, live, under the session's project, folder and branch. When Claude exits, the terminal's row comes back where it was. Sessions started in other terminal apps still show as in a terminal and can be brought in as before.

Fixes and improvements

  • A session's row menu offers Close Terminal when it runs in a Maxwell terminal, instead of Bring into Maxwell

item.title: Panel tabs stay on the edge
item.description:
Every panel now keeps its tab on the window's edge. An open panel's tab is lit. Click it to hide the panel, and click again to bring it back. Tabs no longer disappear when you open the panel they belong to.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed the Viewer tab showing nothing when no file was open

item.title: New sessions start in the right project
item.description:
⌘N now starts with the project. Inside a project, it starts there and ⏎ goes. From All projects nothing is picked until you pick, so a session no longer lands in the folder of whatever you looked at last.

Type a few letters to find any project: the folders your sessions used, and every git repo in the usual places such as ~/projects, ~/Developer and ~/Documents/GitHub, even ones no session has opened yet. ↑ ↓ move, and ⌘O still picks any folder.

Fixes and improvements

  • Maxwell now warns before starting a session in your home folder or a folder outside any project, where Claude would see everything below it

item.title: Groups hold up when sessions get busy
item.description:
Maxwell's groups now hold up when sessions run subagents, background shells and permission prompts. We ran scripted sessions through each case and compared Maxwell with Claude Code's own records every quarter second. Every group change now matches, and you get one notification per real change.

If Maxwell can't read Claude Code's own status for a session, the bottom bar now says ! unverified instead of quietly guessing. Maxwell watch prints every group change as it happens, with where it came from.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed a "done" notification while a subagent or background shell was still running
  • Fixed the vaguer permission notification replacing the exact command a session asked to run
  • Fixed a finished session with a dev server left running staying in Working
  • Fixed file watchers counting as background work
  • Fixed a usage limit from an earlier turn sticking after a clean turn
  • A session that asks the same question again no longer notifies twice

item.title: Viewer tabs that keep your place
item.description:
Going back to a tab now puts you where you were in it. Files keep their scroll position, and the two artifacts you looked at last stay loaded, so switching between them is instant.

A tab that gets something new while you're reading another one shows a purple dot. When the tabs don't fit, ⌄ at the end of the strip lists them all and turns purple when one out of sight is new. ⌥⌘← and ⌥⌘→ step through the tabs, closing one takes you back to the tab you had before, and your tabs come back when Maxwell restarts.

The folder now sits beside the page when the viewer is wide. In a narrow viewer it slides over the page for one pick, so the page keeps its full height.

Fixes and improvements

  • TSV and CSV files now show as a table
  • Squeezed tabs keep their names readable and cut them in the middle, so the extension stays
  • Plain text files wrap, and code in the light theme is easier to read
  • An artifact link inside an artifact now opens as a tab of its own
  • The viewer gets two thirds of the height when it shares the right side with another panel

item.title: Artifact links open beside the session
item.description:
Clicking a claude.ai artifact link in a session's terminal now opens the artifact in the viewer, signed in to that session's account. Before, a plain click went to Claude Code, which opened the link in your default browser, and only ⌘-click reached the viewer.

Other clicks still go to Claude Code as before, and dragging from a link still selects text.

item.title: Settings you can read
item.description:
Every page in Settings has been rewritten in plain words. Each setting now says what it is and what it does for you, with its switch or choice on the right. They're grouped under headings that say what the group is for. "Fold into Idle", "Final model check" and "Glass tint" are now "Move quiet sessions to Idle after", "Check finished work with Haiku" (with what it costs and what turning it off means) and "Opacity".

You can tell a setting's state at a glance. A switch that's off is an empty outline, and Reset shows only when you've changed a value. A theme fixed in your config file greys out the choices it overrides. Hooks are listed per account, and an account that shares another's settings.json says so. Plugins waiting for a key say "Not connected" and which key to paste.

Keys has a filter (⌘F). Projects shows each project's logo next to its name. Uninstalling hooks now asks first.

Fixes and improvements

  • Settings no longer shift sideways when a scrollbar appears
  • Install and uninstall hooks and Restart to Update no longer have a one-click Run button in Keys
  • Advanced › Open guide now opens the settings reference, and the raw config dump is gone

item.title: The viewer has tabs
item.description:
The viewer now keeps each session's files and artifacts in tabs, the way VS Code and Cursor do. Before, it showed one at a time.

A file the session opens goes into the preview tab, shown in italics, and its next file replaces it. Double-click the tab, or press ⌥⌘P, to keep it. While you're reading a tab you kept, new files wait in a tab behind it.

A path you ⌘-click gets a tab of its own. Click × or middle-click to close a tab, or press ⌘W in the viewer. Drag tabs to reorder them, and right-click one for Close Others, Close All, Reveal in Finder and Copy Path.

Fixes and improvements

  • The folder tree no longer squeezes in above an artifact
  • The viewer's ⋯ and × now sit at the panel's right edge, after the tab's own buttons

item.title: Working, Needs you and Your turn you can trust
item.description:
Maxwell now takes each session's group from Claude Code itself. It reads what the process is doing and, for background sessions, how Claude Code says the last turn ended. Before, a session that had asked you to approve something stayed in Working for as long as a background shell it started kept running. It now shows in Needs you, in Claude Code's words: "approve the staging deploy in the dashboard, then tell me".

A session whose turn is over but whose background work is still running stays in Working. A line under its title says what it waits for. Hover that line on any session to see where its group came from. Maxwell state prints the same for every session.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed idle sessions showing as Working when Claude Code expected more work later
  • Fixed questions in a reply's body, such as an Open questions list, putting a session in Needs you when its status line said Safe to close or Not done
  • Needs you now clears when the prompt is answered or the turn ends, even without a hook
  • A turn that ends without a Stop hook (Esc, a queued prompt) no longer stays in Working
  • Sessions in a repo's main checkout no longer fail worktree clean because of other sessions' worktrees in .claude/worktrees

item.title: See the agents a session runs
item.description:
When a session hands work to subagents, Maxwell now shows it. The row says 3 agents (or 1 agent · 2 shells), so a session that sits in Working tells you why.

The header gets a 3 agents button. Hover it for what each agent is doing. Click it, or press ⇧⌘G, and Claude's own agent list opens in the terminal: pick one with ↑ ↓ and ⏎ to read its chat or message it.

Fixes and improvements

  • Safe to close now names what it's waiting for, like "2 subagents and 1 background shell running"

item.title: Terminals sit with your sessions
item.description:
⌥⌘T now opens a terminal inside Maxwell, not in a window of its own. It gets a row under Terminals at the top of the sidebar and runs in the middle pane, like a session. The row shows the folder the shell is in, and follows it when you cd.

Open as many as you like: with new on the Terminals header, from ⌘K, or by right-clicking a session and choosing Open Terminal Here. J K and ⌘[ ⌘] step through them with your sessions. × on the row, ⌘W or exit ends one.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed close all and stop all covering a row after launch
  • Maxwell releases are now built, signed and notarized by GitHub Actions on a clean Mac, one release at a time

item.title: Updates work when Maxwell runs from the DMG
item.description:
If you open Maxwell straight from the DMG without dragging it to Applications first, it runs from a disk macOS won't let it change. Restart to update then reopened the same old version and offered the same update again. Maxwell now installs the update into Applications and opens it from there.

Still on an older version and stuck like this? Quit Maxwell, drag it from the DMG to Applications, and open it from there. Updates work from then on.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed Restart to update reopening the old version when Maxwell ran from the DMG
  • Restart to update now says so when no Applications folder can be written, instead of quitting

item.title: Set up in one place, and All projects adds up
item.description:
With no session open, Maxwell now starts with Set up Maxwell. It checks four things: that Claude Code is installed, the session hooks, a claude.ai sign-in for each account so artifacts open beside the session, and notifications. Each step that's left has one button. Steps tick themselves off as you go, and the list goes away once everything is done. Hide puts it away early. Everything in it is also in Settings.

All projects now lists every session, not only the ones waiting on you. Its count matches the bottom bar. Idle and Recently closed stay folded.

A new Maxwell often finds sessions from days ago that are still running. They fold into Idle, and its new stop all stops the background ones. Conversations are kept, and Undo brings them back. Rows of sessions running in another terminal now say so.

Fixes and improvements

  • A question nobody answered for 3 days now folds into Idle instead of staying in Needs you
  • The Dock badge now counts the Needs you group
  • Maxwell now installs with Homebrew: brew install --cask robinsadeghpour/maxwell/maxwell

item.title: Keep the names you give your sessions
item.description:
If you name your sessions yourself, turn off Settings › General › Sessions › Name sessions for me. Each session then shows what Claude Code shows: the name you gave it with /rename, or its own title. Haiku no longer titles it, and Bring into Maxwell keeps its name. Rename in Maxwell still works. The setting is on by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it off.

Fixes and improvements

  • New config key: auto-titles

item.title: A plain terminal, one key away
item.description:
⌥⌘T opens a plain terminal in the folder of the session you're looking at. Right-click any session and choose Open Terminal Here to open one in that session's folder.

Maxwell now finds claude wherever your shell does. Installs through npm, nvm, Volta or bun keep it outside the usual folders, and Maxwell then listed no background sessions. It now asks your login shell once. If it still can't find claude, it says so when it opens.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed sessions missing from the list when claude was installed with npm, nvm, Volta or bun
  • Maxwell state now prints the claude it uses and any account whose listing failed

item.title: Pick a sound for each notification
item.description:
Settings › General › Notifications now has two notifications, each with its own sound. Needs you is on as before. Turn finished is new: Maxwell tells you when a session stops and the next move is yours. Choose any macOS sound, or None. Picking one plays it.

Neither one shows for the session you're looking at. The notification sound now comes from Maxwell, so if you set up sounds in Claude Code hooks, you can remove them.

When macOS hasn't allowed Maxwell to notify, its notifications show Script Editor's icon and clicking one opens nothing. Settings now says so and opens System Settings › Notifications for you.

Fixes and improvements

  • New config keys: notify-sound, notify-done and notify-done-sound

item.title: Terminal sessions move into Maxwell
item.description:
Bring into Maxwell now ends the session in your terminal before it continues in Maxwell. Recent Claude Code versions stopped recording which process runs a terminal session, so Maxwell couldn't find it, and the session carried on in Warp or Terminal while a second copy started in Maxwell. Maxwell's hook now notes the process itself.

When Claude Code hasn't been told it may work in a folder, ⌘T and New Session now ask Let Claude work in this folder?, the same question Claude asks in a terminal. Click Trust Folder and the session starts.

Slack and Linear now start off. Turn them on in Settings › Plugins when you want them.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed Bring into Maxwell failing for sessions started in the home folder
  • Fixed the "Not trusted on default yet" dead end on ⌘ T
  • Messages name the account only when you have more than one
  • When several Claude sessions run in the same folder and Maxwell can't tell which one to move, it says so and leaves them running
  • Maxwell is now signed and notarized by Apple, so the download opens without the "could not verify" warning. Plugin keys ask for Keychain access once more after this update

item.title: Quieter plugin lists and a tidier Settings
item.description:
The Linear and Slack lists now read like lists. Ticket keys sit in their own dim column, so titles line up. A ticket with nothing to add is one line tall. Status badges are a dot and a word. A row's buttons show when the pointer is on it, so they no longer crowd the text.

Every Settings tab picks its options from one segmented control, and notes wrap instead of being cut off. Each plugin's description reads in full under its switch.

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed × on the System or Usage panel closing both. It now closes only its own panel. The bottom panels together still hide with ⌥⌘J
  • Plugin panel section titles now match the other panel headers
  • Plugin keys no longer ask for Keychain access again after every update. Allow it once more after this update and it sticks
  • New session now lists each project's folder instead of its worktrees, and skips folders that no longer exist
  • Safe to close no longer waits 2 hours. A finished session is safe as soon as every check passes, and the safe-after setting is gone

item.title: Every reply ends with where the session stands
item.description:
Sessions now end each reply with a short status line: Safe to close, Not done or Needs you, and a few words on why. Maxwell shows the line on the session's row, so you can read where every session stands without opening it.

The line is also evidence. Needs you moves the session to Needs you. Not done keeps it out of Safe to close, whatever else passes. Maxwell gives each new session the rule through its SessionStart hook, so nothing changes in your prompts.

Turn it off with wrap-line = off in the config.

Fixes and improvements

  • The installed hook now updates itself when Maxwell updates

item.title: Terminal keys that work like Ghostty
item.description:
The terminal in Maxwell now edits the way Ghostty and Warp do. ⌘⌫ deletes to the start of the line, ⌥⌫ deletes a word, and ⌘V with a screenshot on the clipboard pastes it into Claude as an image.

Close Session moves to ⇧⌘⌫ to make room.

Permission prompts are off for new sessions

Sessions Maxwell starts or brings in now run with --dangerously-skip-permissions instead of auto mode, so they don't stop to ask before every command. Turn it off in Settings › General › Sessions, or with skip-permissions = off in the config.

Fixes and improvements

  • ⌘C in the terminal no longer clears Claude Code's highlighted selection
  • Fixed a white strip covering the title bar in full screen. Tabs, new session, search and settings stay visible
  • Copied files paste as their paths, and files dropped on the terminal paste the same way

item.title: Plugins: Linear and Slack
item.description:
Maxwell now has plugins, and two ship with it. They live in one Plugins panel (⌥⌘6) with a tab each, and dock left, right or bottom like every other panel.

Linear

Each session's ticket and status show on its row, read from the branch name or the transcript. "Linear ticket done" joins the Safe to close checks, so a session isn't safe until its ticket is. When the work moves, Linear suggests the matching ticket move: In Progress when a session starts, a comment when the PR opens, Done when it merges.

Slack

Slack lists who is waiting on a reply from you: DMs, mentions and threads, with bugs and customers first. It only reads. Start Session starts a Claude session from a message and links the two, and that session isn't safe to close until you've replied in the thread.

Write your own

A plugin is a folder with a manifest and a program in any language. It talks to Maxwell with JSON lines over stdin and stdout, and Maxwell draws its panels with its own components, so every plugin looks native in every theme. A plugin that crashes is shown as stopped with a Restart button. It can't take Maxwell down. Read the plugin guide.

Fixes and improvements

  • Connect Slack with ⌘K › Connect Slack…, which opens Slack's app page with the manifest filled in
  • Plugin secrets live in the Keychain and only the plugin that declared them can read them
  • ⇧⌘O opens the selected session's Linear ticket

item.title: Artifacts open beside the session
item.description:
When a session publishes a claude.ai artifact, it now opens on the right, next to the session that made it, signed in as that session's account. Publishing again reloads it in place, even when it's pinned.

Each account signs in once, on claude.ai's own page, and keeps its own login. Maxwell already knows which account every session runs on, so it always picks the right one. ⇧⌘O opens the artifact in that account's browser profile or container instead.

Bring terminal sessions into Maxwell

A session running in another terminal now has a Bring into Maxwell button. Maxwell ends the terminal's process and resumes the same conversation as a background session, with the same id, account, folder and permission mode. A session in the middle of a turn moves when the turn ends. Session › Bring Terminal Sessions into Maxwell… moves all of them at once.

Fixes and improvements

  • Close any session from its right-click menu. If it isn't safe yet, Maxwell says what's still open and asks first
  • Sessions named only by a slug or their first words get a readable name from Haiku, once, for about $0.0003
  • Right-click a session to rename it. Your name always wins

item.title: Maxwell is public
item.description:
Maxwell is a native Mac app for running many Claude Code sessions at once. It reads what every session is doing, sorts them by what they need from you, and only calls a session safe to close when it can prove it.

The first public release covers the core: the six groups, projects on a Dock-style rail, the real Claude session attached in a Ghostty terminal, Markdown files rendered beside it, usage for every account, and search across everything with ⌘P.

Safe to close means safe

Unknown is never safe. A session needs proof that its task is finished: nothing running, two quiet hours, a last message that asks nothing, git clean and pushed, the PR merged. Then Haiku reads the last message once and has to answer finished. Closing only runs claude stop, with Undo for 10 seconds. How Safe to close works.

Fixes and improvements

  • Updates come straight from GitHub's public releases. No GitHub login needed
  • Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later
  • Free and open source under the MIT licence
